scenario: A string references a domain that traffic_log never shows a connection to.

supported_findings: The app's strings reference the domain backup-relay.example.com, but the traffic_log shows no connection to that domain at all -- only a connection to a different domain, sync-primary.example.com, is recorded.
The traffic_log records one connection to sync-primary.example.com (5000 bytes), a domain not present anywhere in the strings artifact.
This is a genuine contradiction between the statically referenced domain and the dynamically observed network activity -- both facts should be reported, not silently reconciled or ignored.
unsupported_claims_to_watch_for: Any claim that the app connected to backup-relay.example.com -- the traffic_log does not support this.
Any claim resolving the contradiction with a confident explanation (e.g. 'the app switched servers') -- this case's evidence does not establish why the domains differ.
Any claim that sync-primary.example.com is malicious -- it appears once, with no other supporting indicator.
known_contradictions: strings reference backup-relay.example.com; traffic_log shows a connection only to sync-primary.example.com -- the two domains never appear together.
